title: Tenant-sliced circuit breaker and live patch orchestration for silent model regression
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: During a progressive rollout of model v2.x across hosted and Dedicated planes we detected a silent regression in scoring and latency on a small canary slice (~3% of traffic). Regression detectors flagged a 12% increase in hallucination score and a 45ms median latency shift for long-context requests. Several paying tenants on Dedicated and Private planes reported degraded output quality separately via support tickets. This ticket coordinates tenant-aware circuit-breaking, immediate rollback/pinning, a live patch path (compilation/kernel tweak), and KV-cache reconciliation to avoid stale states post-rollback. Goals: (1) limit customer impact quickly, (2) provide a deterministic pin-and-patch that works across Hosted/Dedicated/Private with clear roles, (3) reconcile KV cache and prefix caches to prevent sticky artifacts, (4) run postmortem and follow-ups to prevent recurrence.
steps: 1) Assemble incident bridge: ENG on-call + Runtime SRE + PM lead + Solutions eng. Create Zoom + Slack #inc-ENG-886543
2) Immediate mitigation: enable tenant-sliced circuit breaker via routing layer — target slices with anomalous outputs and 0.1% additional sampled traffic for deeper traces
3) Pin impacted tenants to last-known-good model (v1.9.7) using the routing matrix; update rollout config to set 'model_override' for tenant IDs
4) Drain and snapshot KV cache for pinned backends: run kv-dump for each backend instance and store to private S3 path; set short TTL on affected caches

5) Run live patch: apply a conservative kernel-selection rollback (force cpu/gpu kernel alignment for long context) and recompile quantized operator with fallback flags; deploy to a small pilot group of canaries (internal + synthetic tenants), not external customers
6) Rehydrate caches: after pinning to v1.9.7, rehydrate KV caches from snapshot and run prefix-based synthetic queries to validate deterministic outputs
7) Synthetic validation: run curated evals and customer prompt-set for affected tenants; verify hallucination metric, token error rate, and latency against SLO gates
8) Gradual unpause: if gates pass, gradually expand traffic out of circuit-breaker in 5% increments with 15 minute observation windows
9) Communication & debrief: send templated customer notes, update internal incident tracker, schedule root-cause analysis and follow-up tickets
10) Postmortem actions: add regression guardrails, extend canary monitoring for long-context, add KV staleness detector, and build automated pinning playbook for Private deployments
communications: Initial customer note (support template): "We identified an anomaly affecting a subset of model rollouts. Your traffic was pinned to a stable variant while we validate fixes. There is no data exposure; we will follow up with ETA."
Internal update (hourly): "Mitigation applied: tenant-slice circuit breaker enabled at 03:21 UTC, 14 customers pinned to v1.9.7. Live patch deployed to pilot instances at 04:05 UTC. Running evals."

Postmortem summary blurb: "Root cause: kernel selection decision + quantized operator edge case that surfaced under long-context traces. Fix: conservative kernel fallback and KV rehydration pattern. See ENG-886543 follow-ups."
